subject.title: [Bug]: CLI relay exits silently with code 1 when session lane is blocked — no timeout or busy error surfaced

question: Should same-session `openclaw agent` CLI lane waits become a terminal structured busy result, or should the CLI preserve eventual queued execution and only improve diagnostics?
rationale: Current main has the lane-wait facts internally, but surfacing them as `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` changes the user-visible CLI delivery contract and exit-code semantics.

options.title: Land Structured Busy Result
options.body: Repair and land the linked PR direction so CLI callers get actionable stderr and JSON for lane-busy waits while non-CLI Gateway calls stay unopted.

options.title: Keep Queued Execution
options.body: Preserve existing eventual execution semantics and add only clearer progress or timeout diagnostics, accepting less deterministic orchestration behavior.

options.title: Pause For Queue Policy
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide the broader lane-wait behavior across CLI, Gateway, and channels.

recommendation.title: Land Structured Busy Result
recommendation.body: Repair and land the linked PR direction so CLI callers get actionable stderr and JSON for lane-busy waits while non-CLI Gateway calls stay unopted.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the Gateway-backed agent CLI boundary introduced in earlier work by Peter Steinberger and is a product/API contract choice more than a local queue-code fix.
